Much Is Given, Much Is Required
17H.9 The cares and pleasures of this world, and lusts of things, pervert and choke one's faith in the word of God.

precepts.text: Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.
precepts.point: Video played in class touring the Abrahamic Family House in the UAE: a church, a mosque, and a synagogue standing side by side, opened in 2023 to honor the shared values of Islam, Christianity, and Judaism. One thing all three of those religions have in common: they enslaved and destroyed our people. And now they are all trying to get together; it goes right back to what Nimrod did, trying to bring everybody together as one.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Those sown on stony ground hear the word and “immediately receive it with gladness”, but they have no root, and “when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended.” For the word's sake means for teaching the gospel and living the gospel. Christ told us that affliction and persecution would come.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake.” Hated of all nations, for his name's sake. The religions that enslaved and destroyed our people, Christianity, Islam and Judaism, are now coming together side by side, like Nimrod bringing everybody together as one, and the ones hated by all of them are those who hold to the truth of Christ.

“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” Many shall be offended: that is the stony ground. They received the word with gladness, but when the persecution came, they were offended, betrayed their brothers and turned to hate.

It is already written. “In the latter times some shall depart from the faith”, and we are in the latter times now. Some of you, men and women listening, will depart from this faith: some because of persecution, some because they see signs and wonders, technological signs and wonders, and believe we've been wrong all this time. Christ said, “Behold, I have told you before.” He warned us, so that the persecution finds roots in us and not stony ground.

precepts.text: Sown among thorns: the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lust of other things choke the word. Wisdom is free from those cares, so a man with wisdom does not entertain covetousness.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 says wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from what care? Free from worry and stress, and above all free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches and the lusts of other things deceive you. Life does not consist in the abundance of things; they deceive you and choke the word.

Wisdom is free of those cares. The man that has wisdom is not going to be subject to the riches of this world. God said beware of covetousness, and that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it; I am not going to entertain that.

So it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, because wisdom has “all power, overseeing all things.” Tether yourself to wisdom and you can see clearly, the cares of this world cannot choke the word, and it will not become unfruitful in you.

precepts.text: Sown on stony ground: they hear the word and receive it with gladness, I am an Israelite, but have no root, no study, sports and porn first and Bible last, and endure but for a time; when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended. Satan asks to test you where you are weak, and the brother struggling with a proclivity who goes to the gym at two in the morning finds two men in the shower inviting him in; stay out of the gym and do calisthenics at home. Sown among thorns: the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lust of other things, the thing in you that nobody else knows but God, Satan, and you, choke the word.
precepts.point: Matthew 24:10: then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers we broke bread with who stayed in our homes, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight; God will not bless your hands after so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

note.label: War & the Pain of Repentance

precepts.why:
“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas traveled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook Paul. He saw the looseness of the women: Paul, I’ve got to go, my man, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. He let that overcome him. Crescens left for Galatia, Titus for Dalmatia. Mark shows what happened to Paul’s companions, men who were strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Those guys are some of you guys.

“And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness.” I’m an Israelite, we got history, oh I love it. “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time.” No root: I don’t study, I don’t addict myself to the ministry, I like my sports, I like my porn, the Bible comes last. So you only endure this gospel for a time.

“afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” Offended, and you leave. Affliction is things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. That is why Paul told Timothy not to be ashamed of his affliction, to suffer in it with him and stir up the gift within him. Christ lets us know some of us are going to leave this truth because of affliction.

And Satan will test. He asks the Lord, can I test him? Can I test her? The brother with a proclivity for the male gender went to the gym at two in the morning, where the freaks come out at night, found two men in the shower, stood there five whole minutes, and they invited him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, a piece of the American pie, may not be your thing. But the lust of other things is anything in you that nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not tempting you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and asks to tempt you right there.

That is what took Demas, Crescens and Titus, and it is what Paul went through with Alexander the coppersmith, who was in the ministry and turned against it, “for he hath greatly withstood our words.” We have seen the same: men in the gospel who went online to try to tear this down. “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me.” Christ already prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers and sisters we broke bread with, who stayed in our homes and knew our families, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight. God is not going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

precepts.text: The cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things choke the word; those are the promotions Satan offers.
precepts.point: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
Balak said, “I thought to promote thee unto great honour; but, lo, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour.” That was Satan speaking through Balak, trying to entice Balaam with honor to curse Israel.

Satan promotes with honor, riches, prestige, and lust. “And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things are the promotions Satan offers, and they choke the word.

Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up. Resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

precepts.point: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The honor Balak offered was Satan's device against a man who had just spoken the word of the Lord. “And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.”

When the word is sown, Satan comes immediately to take it away, using whatever device fits where you are: honor for Balaam, riches, prestige, or lust for another. He is an old spirit using the same tricks from the beginning of time.

precepts.text: Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.
precepts.point: The good ground hears and understands, and brings others in behind him.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.”

Mark names the wicked one and tells how fast he moves: “And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.” The wicked one is Satan, and he comes immediately. The man on the way side hears the word and does not understand it, and before it can take hold Satan has taken it away.

That is the first of the four grounds. The stony ground receives it with joy and has no root, and is offended when tribulation or persecution arises, which can come through family or through a job. The thorns are the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, which choke the word. The good ground hears and understands, bears fruit, and brings others in behind him. On the way side the word never gets that far; Satan takes it the moment it is heard.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful”: the lust of other things could be power or respect. When you meditate on how you could have lived compared to how you live now, it chokes the word, and the word of God becomes bitter.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: The seed among thorns is people who hear the word, but the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things enter and choke it, leaving it unfruitful. Money and sex are two great stumbling blocks. You can have heard and received the truth and then let these things destroy it. That is how somebody who once had zeal needs to return to the first works.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
Christ gave an example about that thing. “And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” This was the third type of Israelite that Christ mentioned; when you read verse 15 down to 20 there are four categories, and verses 18 and 19 are the third group. This group of Israelites hear the word, and the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, then it says the lusts of other things, because everybody's lust is not money. You might think, oh, it's money; it says the lusts of other things. Some people have a lust for power, some a lust for sex; there is a multitude of various types of lust. And it says entering in choke the word that you had already learned, and it becometh unfruitful.

So that is an example of how you could at one time be alive, but then in time you can become dead. That is what Christ was making reference to in Revelation 3:1-2. And if you don't build yourself up, the cares of the world, the deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things will creep in and choke the word.
